dsid_e728a420a02a4ddcb125e6adb09d211e.semantic_summary: An incident at the SoMa satellite office involved the office edge bridge device (Ubiquiti UBB-Edge v2) being reprovisioned to NAT mode, which caused source IP addresses of VPN client traffic to be rewritten to the bridge's SNAT pool. This rewriting broke VPN policy routing and caused Okta SSO token validation failures, resulting in intermittent 403 errors and timeouts for users on the office Wi-Fi. A postmortem and configuration template updates are planned to prevent recurrence across multiple sites.

Large batch embedding jobs with batch size 256 triggered many short-lived threads, exhausting process thread limits on runtime nodes. The autoscaler lagged in scaling up capacity, worsening the issue. Immediate mitigations included scaling nodes, tenant-level rate limiting, rolling back prefetch config, and deploying a hotfix to enforce backpressure respect and bounded thread pools. Post-fix, error rates returned to baseline within 20 minutes. The incident was mitigated by 19:50 UTC with follow-up actions planned for autoscaler policy and runbook updates.

dsid_426ca69578a84dd4af512e5a2782086e.semantic_summary: This pull request introduces a 'safelock' gating mechanism in the Redwood runtime kernel selection path to prevent fast-path execution unless runtime validators confirm correctness, thereby avoiding silent regressions. It adds a precision toggle API with strict, balanced, and aggressive modes to control numerical precision per model and deployment. The PR also modifies the KV cache eviction policy to be conservative when cache warmness is low, integrates safelock signals with the continuous-batching scheduler to prefer conservative batching until validators succeed, and adds observability metrics and dashboards. Testing includes unit, integration, and stochastic edge-case tests. Operator guidance and migration notes ensure backward compatibility and safe rollout. The feature is enabled by default for new deployments with options to opt out or opt into aggressive precision modes. Performance benchmarks show a small initial throughput cost that improves after validator warm-up, with aggressive mode offering throughput gains at a slight correctness tradeoff.

dsid_fa2d9f0bda0e4d6b9174ae6b15f7b37e.semantic_summary: This Slack conversation in the eng-infra channel documents a network incident involving intermittent packet loss and interface flaps on ToR switch tor-04 affecting traffic between racks 4a and 4b. The internal L4 load balancer VIPs gen-infer-01 and gen-infer-02 experienced backend healthcheck failures and connection resets. Investigation revealed MTU and ECN related packet fragmentation and truncation issues likely caused by hardware bugs on tor-04. Network engineers ran diagnostic commands, captured pcaps, and performed iperf3 tests confirming path MTU blackhole behavior. Temporary mitigations included disabling ECN and applying MTU clamps on load balancer frontends, which improved retransmit rates. A ticket (NET-1983) was created to track the suspected hardware bug, and a follow-up ticket (INFRA-447) was opened to replace the tor-04 linecard and test vendor firmware patches. Monitoring and alerting improvements were also planned.
